messages:
brooke: Trying the Windows quickstart in a corp VM. The sample prints '401 Unauthorized' on the first call. When I run curl from the VM I get a JSON: {"error":"billing_required","message":"workspace needs billing setup"}. That's confusing.
alejandro: Is the VM behind a corporate NTLM proxy? Windows often uses Integrated Auth which returns 407 before TLS. What does curl -v show?
brooke: curl -v output:
* Connected to proxy.local (10.1.1.5) port 8080 (#0)
> CONNECT api.play.redwood.ai:443 HTTP/1.1
> Proxy-Authorization: NTLM TlRMTVNTUAAB...
< HTTP/1.1 407 Proxy Authentication Required
< Proxy-Authenticate: NTLM
So proxy is returning 407. But the quickstart app only logs '401 Unauthorized' which made me rotate keys.
anna: That matches other reports: transport-level proxy auth (407) gets swallowed by the SDK retry logic and later the backend returns billing_required which then surfaces. Two different errors get merged into a generic auth failure.
brooke: Repro steps I used: in corp VM with NTLM proxy enabled, run the Windows quickstart EXE -> first-call fails with '401'. Then run: curl -v -x http://proxy.local:8080 https://api.play.redwood.ai/v1/health -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -> shows 407. If I run curl without proxy it shows billing_required JSON.
alejandro: Action items: 1) add a "Windows / corporate proxy" troubleshooting snippet to quickstart README with curl -v examples and how to pass creds to dotnet/curl, 2) change SDK to preserve transport-level HTTP codes (407) in logs and show both transport and backend bodies on first-call failures.
brooke: Workaround I used: run quickstart with system proxy disabled or run from home network, or create a split-tunnel so api.play.redwood.ai bypasses corp proxy. Also accept the org trial billing in the console to avoid billing_required.
devex-bot: new issue created: DEVEX-1190 "windows quickstart: corporate NTLM proxy + billing gate cause confusing 401" assigned to alejandro
